title: Review findings
description: ONE findings shape for both review tracks. All six external reviewers of 9.18.1 converged on a single ask: the R2 gate hand-parses Markdown and carries `unbalanced-fence` and `malformed-row` as first-class violation kinds — i.e. it has defect classes FOR ITS OWN PARSER. This schema is deliberately NOT a new format: it is the shape `self_review_gate.ts` already emits under `--findings-out` and `check_finding_dispositions.ts` already hand-validates in code, lifted into a file both tracks can point at. Inventing a second JSON shape here would have been the exact fragmentation the reviewers complained about.

schema_version.description: Pinned. `check_finding_dispositions.parse_ledger` already rejects anything else, so this is a promotion of an existing check rather than a new constraint. Spelled as a one-member `enum` rather than `const`: the repo's own Draft-07 subset validator (validate_frontmatter.ts) enforces `enum` and silently ignores `const`, so `const` here would have been a pin nothing checked.

release.description: Version the ledger belongs to. Present on the release-findings ledger (agents/evidence/release-findings/<version>.json); absent on a bare --findings-out emission, which is why it is not required here.

review_independence.description: Whether the reviewer set spans more than one model family. Added because the artifact was previously silent on it: the self-review gate calls ONE Anthropic client, and the ledger it wrote was byte-indistinguishable from one backed by independent models — so a consumer read 'no findings' as acceptance either way. `unknown` is an honest value for a set that was not recorded, NOT a synonym for cross-family.

acceptance_status.description: What a consumer may claim this artifact establishes. DERIVED from `review_independence` (see _lib/review_independence.ts), never set independently: two fields a producer can set inconsistently reintroduce exactly the ambiguity the pair removes, and a same-family set carrying `accepted` would still read as acceptance to anyone scanning one field. Only `cross-family` yields `accepted`; `unknown` yields `provisional`, because an unrecorded member set is not evidence of independence.

assurance.description: How much INDEPENDENT evidence backs the verdict — deliberately orthogonal to how much effort the review spent. Collapsing the two is the mechanism by which a long, careful, single-model pass reads as acceptance: effort is visible in the artifact (finding count, detail, rationale) and independence is not, so a reader with only one axis substitutes the one they can see. A five-hour same-family review is `single-pass`; a terse two-family one is `independent`.

reviewers.description: The member names the independence verdict was derived from, recorded so the derivation is auditable rather than asserted. Provider names as `ai_council/config.ts::_VALID_PROVIDERS` spells them.

findings.description: May be empty. An empty array is an honest null, not a missing field — the distinction the Markdown track spells with its own §2.3 line. The item shape is INLINED rather than `$ref`-ed for the same measured reason: the subset validator does not resolve `$ref`, so a referenced definition would have validated nothing.

finding_id.description: First 12 hex of sha256(`kind|title|file`), per findingId() in self_review_gate.ts. Stable across runs, which is what lets the disposition ledger key on it. NOT required: an in-flight finding may not have been keyed yet, and requiring it would make the schema reject the shape the model returns before the gate stamps it. It is a FINDING id, NOT a commit SHA — a 12-hex string looks exactly like a short SHA, and searching the commit log for it finds nothing by design; the disposition lives in agents/evidence/release-findings/<version>.json.

severity.description: The JSON track's four levels. The Markdown track's own severity vocabulary is a superset in spirit but a different list; mapping between them is a caller's job, not this schema's — see the mapping note in the description of `kind`.

kind.description: Finding class. Load-bearing for the id: findingId() hashes kind|title|file, so a kind change is a new finding rather than an edit of the old one.

title.description: Truncated at 300 by parseFindings() in self_review_gate.ts; the bound is pinned here so a producer cannot emit a title the consumer will silently cut.

detail.description: Truncated at 2000 by parseFindings(). Same reasoning as `title`.

file.description: Repo-relative path. Optional because a finding can be about the change as a whole; findingId() folds an absent file to the empty string so the id stays stable either way.

status.description: Disposition. `fixed` / `false_positive` / `accepted_risk` are the three terminal states check_finding_dispositions accepts; `open` is the initial state. NOTE the underscore spelling — the Markdown track writes `accepted-risk` with a hyphen in its Status cell, and the two vocabularies are deliberately not unified here: renaming either would break committed artefacts on that track.

rationale.description: Why the disposition. Required by check_finding_dispositions for a non-`fixed` terminal status; enforced there rather than here because the requirement is conditional on the workflow stage, not on the document.

verified_by.description: Who or what confirmed the disposition.

date.description: ISO calendar date of the disposition.
